messages:
incident-bot: [ALERT] spike detected on /auth/refresh 2026-11-02T03:42:10Z - >4k requests in 10m, elevated 401s, unusual client_id spread. paging on-call.
alice: acknowledged. i'm looking. who can grab recent refresh logs and unique token ids?
maria: pulling: `kubectl logs deploy/auth -n prod --since=20m | grep refresh_token | tail -n 500`
maria: sample: `2026-11-02T03:36:21Z INFO refresh_token user=usr_83 client_id=mobile-v2 ip=54.210.22.11 status=200 age=9d` 
`2026-11-02T03:37:02Z WARN refresh_token client_id=mobile-v2 ip=54.210.22.11 status=401 reason=invalid_sig`
ajay: pattern: many 401s and a bunch of successful 200s from same ASN 54.210.22.0/24. Looks like someone replaying valid refresh tokens and brute forcing others.
sam: rate observed ~95 rps to /auth/refresh from that /24, mostly header X-Client-Id: mobile-v2. No increased 5xx on generation services.
lee: customer impact quick check: edge gateways show user-facing 401s spiking for mobile sessions; estimated ~1.2% active mobile users may get forced re-login during their background refresh. No outage otherwise.
security-bot: audit: no KMS key rotations in last 60d. Checking S3 archives for debug-level dumps.
opsbot: suggestion: apply L7 throttling at edge for /auth/refresh when client_id=mobile-v2; do not blanket drop entire /24.
alice: agree. do targeted rate-limit first to avoid collateral damage. also investigate whether any debug logging leaked tokens.
maria: found an S3 upload from 2026-10-31 04:12 UTC with `auth-debug.log.gz` in bucket `prod-sandbox-logs`. File contains lines that include `refresh_token=` values. That file was produced by a canary deploy that had DEBUG_AUTH env var enabled by mistake.
ajay: i can confirm there was a CI job `deploy/canary/debug-auth` that toggled DEBUG_AUTH=true on one replica on 2026-10-31 04:10Z. It should have been gated. Possible source of leaked tokens.
sam: mitigation plan: 1) edge L7 rate-limit for offending client_id/IPs 2) identify leaked token ids and revoke specific refresh tokens 3) perform signing key rotation with dual-acceptance window 4) CS advisory draft and support triage.
opsbot: proposed rate-limit config (applied as nginx snippet):
```
map $http_x_client_id $is_mobile_v2 {
  default 0;
  "mobile-v2" 1;
}
limit_req_zone $binary_remote_addr zone=rl:10m rate=30r/s; # per-ip
server {
  location /auth/refresh {
    if ($is_mobile_v2) {
      limit_req zone=rl burst=40 nodelay;
    }
  }
}
```
opsbot: applying to prod edge via CD pipeline in 2m (canary first).
alice: hold on full block. remember CDN and partner infra in that ASN. only per-ip rate-limit with a conservative threshold.
maria: after canary rollout, traffic from 54.210.22.11 dropped from 88rps to ~22rps. 401s reduced but replay attempts continue.
lee: digging into leaked file: it lists ~3.9k distinct refresh identifiers referencing user ids across many tenants. We can revoke by id rather than global token purge.
ajay: revoke script ready: `./tools/revoke_refresh_ids.py --input leaked_ids.txt --concurrency 20` - includes dry-run flag.
sam: run dry-run and verify no unexpected failures.
opsbot: dry-run output: would mark 3897 tokens revoked, 0 simulated failures.
alice: proceed with targeted revocation. notify support and include re-login guidance.
security-bot: recommend rotating the refresh token signing key and enabling a 24h acceptance window for previously-signed tokens, to minimize customer impact. Create new KMS key and update services to sign with new key while accepting old for 24h.
ajay: starting revocations at 03:58Z.
maria: revocation progress: 1k/3897 done; auth-service reporting fewer successful refreshes from known compromised ids. Background refresh failures expected for those users; they will be asked to re-auth.
lee: creating CS template: short note explaining forced re-login for some users, we rotated keys for security, recommended steps for customers, link to status page.
sam: handoff plan: i'm leaving in 25m. @lee take on-call at 04:30Z. ensure key rotation finishes or abort safely.
incident-bot: oncall handoff scheduled: sam -> lee at 04:31:00Z
opsbot: starting key rotation runbook step 1: create new KMS key alias `redwood-auth-rtk-v2` and stage deploy.
ajay: implementing dual-sign: services will sign new refresh tokens with new key and accept tokens signed by old key for 12h to 24h. We'll log acceptance to monitor lingering usage.
security-bot: also file compliance ticket and prepare internal incident timeline doc. collect S3 object, CI job metadata, and deploy audit trail.
alice: CS-exec: prepare short advisory but hold until we confirm revocation scope and rotation schedule. we will send an advisory only if >5% users affected or key rotation invalidates tokens widely.
maria: revocation complete at 04:08Z. auth-service logs show reduced replay attempts from leaked ids. overall refresh RPS from ASN dropped ~80%.
lee: rotation started 04:15Z. pushing new key and rolling auth-service. acceptance of old key set to 12h initially. monitoring for errors.
support-bot: opened support queue #4321 to track customer reports. tagging priority: P2.
sam: status before handoff: mitigations applied, targeted revocation done, key rotation in progress, customer impact limited to ~1.2% mobile users. ready to hand off.
incident-bot: handoff executed: sam -> lee at 04:31:00Z
lee: i'm oncall. monitoring rotation. will post updates every 30m or on any regression. created PD incident P2-1771234567.
alice: action items for postmortem (owners): - disable DEBUG_AUTH in prod via deploy guard (maria) - enforce CI gating for DEBUG flags (eng-infra) - scrub auth tokens on upload (eng-sre) - add alert: refresh_token volume per ip and per client_id (eng-platform) - update runbook for targeted token revocation (security).
lee: update 05:05Z - rotation complete, new key active, old key acceptance window set to 12h. observed re-login rate ~1.3% on mobile-v2. support queue minimal, no escalations. moving to monitoring/observation phase.
incident-bot: incident state -> mitigated at 05:10Z (conditions stable).
lee: closing active mitigation but keeping incident doc open for postmortem drafting and follow-ups. assigning owners in tracker.
alice: thanks everyone. concise updates only from now. escalate to P1 if token reuse resumes at scale.
security-bot: opened security advisory draft and compliance ticket referencing S3 upload, CI job id, and list of leaked ids.
maria: final note: scrubbed the S3 object and added lifecycle policy to prevent debug artifacts leaving canaries. will follow up with a PR to CI templates.
sam: good containment. handing off to lee.
lee: will run a 24h watch and post summary. closing thread once postmortem scheduled.
